title: Goalkeeper Basics
description: Learn the keeper habits that help the whole team stay calm and organized.

questions.question: What is a good goalkeeper ready position before a shot?
options: Feet set, knees bent, hands ready
questions.explanation: A set, balanced body helps the keeper move quickly in any direction.

questions.question: When should a goalkeeper get set?
options: As the shooter is about to strike the ball
After the shot is already past them
questions.explanation: Being still and balanced right before the shot gives the keeper the best chance to save it.

questions.question: What should a goalkeeper do after making a save but not holding the ball?
options: Recover quickly and look for the rebound
questions.explanation: Many goals come from rebounds, so the keeper must get up and be ready again.

questions.question: If a shot is coming straight at the keeper, what is usually safest?
options: Catch it or block it into a safe area
questions.explanation: If the keeper can catch cleanly, catch it. If not, push it away from danger.

questions.question: Where can the goalkeeper use their hands?
questions.explanation: A keeper may use hands inside their own penalty area, not outside it.

questions.question: A teammate passes the ball back with their foot. What should the goalkeeper usually do?
options: Use their feet to control or pass it
Pick it up with their hands
questions.explanation: On a deliberate foot pass from a teammate, the keeper should not pick it up.

questions.question: Why should a keeper talk loudly and clearly?
options: To organize defenders and warn about danger
questions.explanation: The keeper sees the whole field, so clear calls help defenders mark, step, and clear.

questions.question: What is the best call when a keeper is coming to catch a cross?
questions.explanation: A loud 'Keeper!' tells defenders to protect space and avoid getting in the way.

questions.question: On a cross, when should the keeper come out?
options: When they are sure they can reach the ball safely
Only if a parent says so
questions.explanation: A keeper should attack crosses they can win. If they cannot reach it, they should stay set.

questions.question: In a 1v1 breakaway, what should the goalkeeper try to do?
options: Stay big, close the angle, and delay the shot
Slide from far away every time
questions.explanation: Closing the angle makes the goal look smaller and gives defenders time to recover.

questions.question: What does 'protect the near post' mean?
options: Do not leave an easy shot between you and the closer post
Stand in the middle no matter what
questions.explanation: The keeper must cover the closest side first because that shot is often quickest.

questions.question: What should a keeper do after catching the ball?
options: Look up and choose a safe distribution
Throw it away quickly without looking
Drop it in front of goal
questions.explanation: A calm keeper can start the next attack with a smart throw, roll, or pass.

questions.question: In the diagram, what should the keeper usually choose if player A is open and close?
questions.imageAlt: Goalkeeper distribution options with a short open teammate
options: Blast it straight at the opponent
questions.explanation: A short open teammate is usually the safest way to keep the ball and build play.

questions.question: When is a long clearance a smart choice?
options: When short options are marked and danger is close
Every time the keeper has the ball
questions.explanation: If the team is under heavy pressure, clearing long can protect the goal.

questions.question: What is a good keeper habit on corner kicks?
options: Start in a strong position and talk before the kick
questions.explanation: Before the kick, the keeper should organize marks and be ready for the cross.

questions.question: If a shot is too hard to catch cleanly, where should the keeper try to push it?
options: Wide or away from the middle
questions.explanation: Pushing wide makes rebounds harder for attackers to finish.

questions.question: What should defenders do when their keeper has the ball?
options: Spread out and offer safe passing options
questions.explanation: Good spacing helps the keeper pass instead of just kicking long.

questions.question: What does it mean for a keeper to be brave but smart?
options: Attack balls they can win and stay safe when they cannot
questions.explanation: Good goalkeeping is about good decisions, not just big dives.

questions.question: If the ball is rolling slowly toward the box with an attacker chasing, what should the keeper think first?
options: Can I get there first safely?
Can I wait on the line?
Can I pick it up anywhere?
questions.explanation: The keeper should judge distance and speed before deciding to come out.

questions.question: What is the keeper's main job?
options: Stop goals and help the team stay organized
questions.explanation: A keeper protects the goal, communicates, and helps the team start attacks.
